summary.intent: Deploy v0.25.0 to staging after merging a release PR, then investigate and fix IPNS publish slowness and broken token refresh on staging.
summary.outcome: Unblocked staging deployment by manually tagging v0.25.1 and fixing a release-please title pattern misconfiguration. Fixed IPNS publish latency via fire-and-forget DHT publish. Initiated a large API client consolidation refactor (PR #309) to eliminate the dual orval codegen and three HTTP client paths in the web app.

repo: The staging deployment workflow triggers on tags matching `v*-staging*`, not release tags — staging deploy always requires a separate manual 'Tag Staging Release' action.

release-please's `pull-request-title-pattern` must include `${component}` for multi-package monorepos, otherwise it cannot match merged PRs back to their components and aborts with 'untagged, merged release PRs outstanding'.

The web app had two separate orval code generations from the same OpenAPI spec: `packages/api-client` (axios, for SDK/desktop consumers) and `apps/web/src/api/` (react-query, for the web app). In practice, almost no react-query hooks were used — most code imported raw generated functions.

Three separate HTTP client paths existed in the web app: orval fetch mutator (`custom-instance.ts`), hand-written axios client (`lib/api/client.ts`), and IPFS functions. Only the axios client had a 401 refresh interceptor.

The API is a zero-knowledge server that never handles plaintext — it stores opaque blobs and proxies IPFS, so `apps/api` genuinely has no workspace package dependencies. The stale `packages/crypto` COPY in the Dockerfile was a leftover.
`IpnsService.publishRecord()` was awaiting delegated routing DHT publish via someguy sidecar, but `resolveRecord()` always prefers the DB cache, making the wait unnecessary.
Grafana Cloud free-tier instances hibernate after inactivity and return HTTP 503 on wake — transient, not a real deployment failure.

code.finding: DHT publish via delegated routing is fire-and-forget — awaiting it caused 30s+ latency. Changed to detached promise with trailing .catch() logging errors via this.logger.error.
Had a stale COPY of packages/crypto/package.json that pulled in @cipherbox/core as a lockfile dependency even though the API has no workspace package deps. Removing it fixed the Docker build.
pull-request-title-pattern was `chore: release` without `${component}`, breaking multi-package release matching after the config was expanded to a monorepo setup.
Entire web-app orval config (react-query mode) was removed as part of consolidation — ~8800 lines of generated code eliminated.
Updated to support refreshAccessToken callback, withCredentials, and onRefreshFailure in ApiClientConfig, with 401 interceptor and shared-promise deduplication for concurrent refresh.
CI workflow had a format/verify step referencing apps/web/src/api/ which no longer exists after the api-client consolidation — needed to be removed.

workflow: When release-please is stuck due to untagged PRs, manually creating the git tag and GitHub release unblocks future runs.
`chore` commits do not trigger release-please version bumps — use `fix` for broken build fixes to get a patch release.
The 'Tag Staging Release' action checks out the release tag's commit, so fixes must be in a release tag — merging to main alone is insufficient.
Spawning parallel debug agents for independent issues (IPNS slowness vs token refresh) is an effective pattern for context isolation.
Codecov patch coverage failures can appear from newly added `.catch()` error handler lines — requires dedicated test coverage for the error path.

friction: release-please aborted silently on PR #306 merge with a non-obvious error about untagged PRs — required digging through workflow logs to find the root cause.
The missing `${component}` in the title pattern was a latent misconfiguration from when the repo was migrated to multi-package release-please — not caught until a real release cycle.
Three separate HTTP client paths in the web app with only one having token refresh created a hard-to-diagnose 401 failure that only manifested during long-running sessions.
Grafana Cloud 503 on wake caused a false alarm on the staging deployment pipeline.
open_items: PR #309 (api-client consolidation refactor) needs CI fix merged and review — the `apps/web/src/api/` reference in ci.yml was addressed in a follow-up commit.
PR #308 (IPNS fire-and-forget fix) needs merge before re-running Tag Staging Release with v0.25.1.
PR #307 (release-please title pattern fix) needs merge to ensure future releases are tagged correctly.

The token refresh fix from the debugger agent was stashed/discarded in favor of the full api-client consolidation refactor — need to verify the new api-client interceptor in PR #309 fully covers the refresh behavior.
Staging deployment of v0.25.1 not yet complete — pending merges of #308 and #309, plus re-running Tag Staging Release.
